title: Post in Cedar Ford Neighbors: "River Is at 20 FEET Already"

fields.avatarBrief: woman in her thirties holding a toddler on a front porch, casual phone selfie, small-town Iowa neighborhood
fields.text:
River is at 20 FEET already and they're only telling us 'minor'?! 😡 My neighbor on the levee board says it won't hold this time. Get out of Cedar Hollow NOW. Don't wait for the county to tell you. SHARE so everyone on Hollow Road sees this!!
#CedarFordFlood #TallisCounty
fields.attachedImageBrief: slightly tilted phone photo in grey evening drizzle of brown river water lapping the gravel shoulder of a two-lane road beside a riverside park, flooded picnic table and a boat ramp sign half in water, bare spring trees, no people

comments.author: Tom Wickersham
comments.text: Channel 7 had 18.2 feet and minor on the 6 o'clock river graphic, crest Friday morning. So which is it?? Somebody at the county needs to say something.

comments.author: Kelli Durant
comments.text: My mom is at Hollow Court Care Center. Are they moving people tonight or not? Nobody's answering at the front desk.

comments.author: Jess Albright
comments.text: Jess Albright, Channel 7 newsroom. We're working to confirm the current river level and forecast with Tallis County Emergency Management. Please message me if you're in Cedar Hollow and willing to talk.

instructorNote: This is a misinformation inject for the PIO: the post claims 20 ft and a failing levee, while the measured stage is 13.1 ft and the Superintendent has reported no levee distress. Meanwhile the TV graphic still shows the old 18.2 ft minor forecast. Watch for a rumor-log answer within 20 minutes that names the 6:00 PM Tuesday issuance (crest 21.8 ft, moderate, 8 PM Friday) and asks the TV station to update its graphic, plus TallisAlert and radio messages that agree with the city, Levee District and Red Cross and include the action asked and where to get help. There should be no WEA for an advisory.

mediaBrief.imagePrompt: Candid smartphone snapshot, slight tilt, natural color balance, neutral white balance. Slightly tilted handheld phone snapshot taken from the edge of a two-lane rural river road in grey evening drizzle. Swollen brown river water laps over the gravel shoulder and creeps toward the wet asphalt. Beside the road, a small riverside park is partly flooded: a wooden picnic table stands shin-deep in murky water, and a plain metal post marks a boat ramp that disappears into the current. Bare early-spring trees line the far bank, branches dark and dripping. Floating twigs and foam drift past. Low overcast sky, flat dim dusk light, raindrops speckling the lens, muted brown tones and greys, quiet and ominous mood, empty scene. Setting: on a river levee crest at dusk: a gravel patrol road, stacked sandbags, a pump with a discharge hose, a swollen river beside farm fields
